s:
Match List-I (Body) with List-II (Year of setting up):
List-I | List-II
a. ECGC | i. 1956
b. STC | ii. 1963
c. MMTC | iii. 1996
d. India Brand Equity Fund | iv. 1957
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ECGC – 1957 (export credit-risk insurer); STC – 1956 (canalising agency for bulk goods); MMTC – 1963 (minerals and metals); IBEF – 1996 (trust of the Department of Commerce).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. EXIM Bank, set up under an Act of 1981 and headquartered in Mumbai, provides lines of credit and buyer's/seller's credit.
2. Export credit-risk insurance is the principal function of EXIM Bank.
3. DGFT, which issues Foreign Trade Policy authorisations, is an attached office of the Department of Commerce at Vanijya Bhavan, New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: EXIM Bank finances foreign trade (lines of credit, buyer's/seller's credit, project exports) and is not an insurer – export credit insurance is ECGC's role.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NIRVIK (Niryat Rin Vikas Yojana), announced in the Budget 2020-21, is an ECGC scheme giving exporters higher insurance cover at a lower premium.
2. Under the present Foreign Trade Policy, status holders are recognised as One-Star to Five-Star Export Houses.
3. Enforcing pre-shipment inspection and quality control of exportable goods is an objective of ECGC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: pre-shipment inspection and quality control are the work of the Export Inspection Council, not an ECGC objective.

s:
Match List-I (Scheme) with List-II (Purpose):
List-I | List-II
a. EPCG | i. Reward for services exports
b. Advance Authorisation | ii. Zero-duty import of capital goods against an export obligation
c. RoSCTL | iii. Duty-free import of inputs for export production
d. SEIS | iv. Rebate for apparel and made-ups
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: EPCG – zero-duty capital goods against an export obligation; Advance Authorisation – duty-free inputs for export production; RoSCTL (replaced RoSL) – apparel and made-ups; SEIS – services exports reward under FTP 2015-20 (MEIS was for goods).

s:
Consider the following statements about the RoDTEP scheme:
1. It replaced the MEIS, which had been challenged at the WTO.
2. It refunds unrebated central, state and local taxes on exported products.
3. It is run online by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: RoDTEP is run online by CBIC, not DGFT.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Export Promotion Mission:
1. It has an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for FY 2025-26 to 2030-31.
2. It is run by the DGFT.
3. It merges the Interest Equalisation Scheme and the RoDTEP scheme.
4. It is meant mainly for MSMEs and first-time exporters.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Mission merges the Interest Equalisation Scheme and the Market Access Initiative, not RoDTEP.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Foreign Trade Policy 2023 came into force on 1 April 2023 and has no fixed end date.
2. The Foreign Trade Policy 2015-20 was extended up to 31 March 2022.
3. The Foreign Trade Policy 2023 targets exports of US$ 2 trillion by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: FTP 2015-20 was extended to 31 March 2023, after which FTP 2023 took over from 1 April 2023.

s:
With reference to the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, consider the following statements:
1. It shifts from incentives towards remission and entitlement-based support.
2. It offers a one-time amnesty for export-obligation defaults under the EPCG and SEIS schemes.
3. It promotes rupee trade settlement and merchanting trade.
4. 'Districts as Export Hubs' is one of its pillars.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the one-time amnesty covers defaults under EPCG and Advance Authorisation; SEIS belonged to FTP 2015-20.

s:
Arrange the following trade policies of India in chronological order:
1. First EXIM Policy
2. Five-year EXIM Policy of 1992
3. First 'Foreign Trade Policy' aiming at 1.5% of world merchandise trade
4. FTP aiming to raise India's share of world exports from 2% to 3.5%
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: First EXIM Policy 1985-88; EXIM Policy 1992 (1992-97); FTP 2004-09 (first 'Foreign Trade Policy', 1.5% target by 2009); FTP 2015-20 (2% to 3.5%). The FTP name came only in 2004, not 1991.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): India's Foreign Trade Policy is administered through the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.
Reason (R): The DGFT is an attached office of the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, which frames the Foreign Trade Policy.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: the FTP is framed by the Department of Commerce (Ministry of Commerce and Industry) and administered through its attached office, the DGFT.

s:
Match List-I (Export-import document) with List-II (Purpose):
List-I | List-II
a. Indent | i. Customs document for clearing export goods
b. Shipping bill | ii. Shipping company's receipt and document of title
c. Mate's receipt | iii. Importer's order to buy goods
d. Bill of lading | iv. Ship's mate acknowledges goods loaded on board
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Indent – importer's order (the import process begins with it); shipping bill – customs clearance of exports; mate's receipt – ship's mate acknowledges loading; bill of lading – shipping company's receipt and document of title.

s:
Match List-I (Stage of economic integration) with List-II (Feature):
List-I | List-II
a. Free Trade Area | i. Free internal trade plus a common external tariff
b. Customs union | ii. Free internal trade; members keep their own external tariffs
c. Common market | iii. Common market plus coordinated economic policies
d. Economic union | iv. Customs union plus free movement of factors
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: FTA – free internal trade, own external tariffs; customs union – adds a common external tariff; common market – adds free movement of factors; economic union – adds coordinated economic policies.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The APEDA Act was passed in December 1985 and came into force in 1986.
2. APEDA functions under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
3. APEDA is the nodal agency for Agri Export Zones, while MPEDA handles marine products.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: APEDA is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Agriculture Export Policy 2018 aimed to double agricultural exports to about $60 billion by 2022.
2. PM Gati Shakti was launched in 2022 and the National Logistics Policy in 2021 to cut logistics costs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the years are swapped – PM Gati Shakti came in 2021 and the National Logistics Policy in 2022.

s:
Consider the following statements about the LEADS 2025 index:
1. It is released by NITI Aayog.
2. Andhra Pradesh was placed in the 'Accelerator' category among coastal states.
3. Tamil Nadu was placed in the 'Exemplar' category among coastal states.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: LEADS (Logistics Ease Across Different States) is released by DPIIT.

s:
Consider the following statements about Special Economic Zones:
1. The SEZ policy was announced on 1 April 2000 and the SEZ Act was enacted in 2005.
2. The SEZ concept was first proposed in the EXIM Policy 1992-97.
3. An SEZ is a duty-free enclave treated as foreign territory for trade and tariff purposes.
4. Asia's first Export Processing Zone was set up at Kandla in 1965.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the SEZ concept came from the EXIM Policy 1997-2002.

s:
Consider the following statements about EOUs, EHTPs and STPs:
1. They must be located within a Special Economic Zone.
2. They are required to export all of their output.
3. EHTPs cover electronics hardware and STPs cover software.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: EOUs, EHTPs and STPs can be located anywhere and need not be in an SEZ.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The SEZ policy sought to give exporters an internationally competitive and hassle-free environment.
Reason (R): 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route for most manufacturing in SEZs.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true (SEZ aims: exports, investment, employment, competitive hassle-free environment; 100% FDI automatic for most manufacturing), but the FDI rule does not explain the policy's aim.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Districts as Export Hubs initiative:
1. Each district plan prioritises 2-3 high-potential products or services.
2. By 2025, export products had been identified in 590 districts and action plans prepared for 734.
3. Srikakulam is one of Andhra Pradesh's priority districts in the 90-day campaign from 1 June 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. 2 reverses the numbers: products were identified in 734 districts, action plans in 590. 3 is wrong: AP's priority districts are Ananthapur, Chittoor, East Godavari, Guntur, Krishna and Visakhapatnam – not Srikakulam.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The IMF's BPM6 presents the Balance of Payments in three accounts – current, capital and financial.
2. The RBI generally combines the capital and financial accounts under 'Capital Account'.
3. The Balance of Trade is the complete record of a country's economic transactions with the rest of the world.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the BoT covers goods only (exports minus imports of goods); the complete record is the Balance of Payments.

s:
Match List-I (Transaction) with List-II (Place in India's BoP):
List-I | List-II
a. Software services exports | i. Capital account
b. NRI deposits such as FCNR(B) | ii. Current account – primary income
c. Private remittances | iii. Current account – secondary income
d. Interest, dividends and profits | iv. Current account – services
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Software exports – current account (services); FCNR(B) NRI deposits – capital account (banking capital); private remittances – secondary income (transfers); interest, dividends, profits – primary income.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's Balance of Payments:
1. The current account includes the Balance of Trade.
2. Foreign Direct Investment is recorded in the current account.
3. Shipping, banking, tourism and software are non-factor services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: FDI, like foreign loans and portfolio investment, is a capital-account item.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Current balance + capital balance + financial balance + net errors and omissions = zero.
2. Like the BoP, the Balance of Trade must always balance.
3. Official reserve changes and official borrowing are autonomous ('above the line') transactions.
4. A positive overall BoP adds to forex reserves, a negative one draws them down.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the BoP always balances in accounting terms but the BoT need not. 3 is wrong: reserve changes and official borrowing are accommodating ('below the line') transactions.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The purchase of foreign assets by residents is recorded as a debit in the capital account.
Reason (R): In the BoP every inflow of foreign exchange is recorded on the debit side.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: buying foreign assets means foreign exchange flows out, a capital-account debit. R is false: every inflow is a credit; outflows are debits.

s:
Arrange the following steps in India's exchange-rate history in chronological order:
1. Rupee delinked from the pound sterling
2. FERA enacted
3. LERMS dual exchange rate (40% official, 60% market)
4. Acceptance of IMF Article VIII
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: FERA 1973; rupee delinked from sterling September 1975; LERMS in the 1992-93 Budget; Article VIII accepted August 1994.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The rupee is fully convertible on the current account but not on the capital account.
2. India accepted Article VIII of the IMF, which makes current account convertibility obligatory, in August 1994.
3. FEMA was enacted in 1999 and came into force on 1 June 2001.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: FEMA came into force on 1 June 2000, replacing FERA.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The High Level Committee on Balance of Payments (1991-93) regarded a current account deficit of about 1.6% of GDP as sustainable.
2. The same committee recommended a market-determined exchange rate.
3. The 1997 Committee on Capital Account Convertibility was chaired by C. Rangarajan.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 1997 (and 2006) Committee on Capital Account Convertibility was chaired by S.S. Tarapore; Rangarajan chaired the BoP committee.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): FERA 1973 was a civil law concerned with the management of foreign exchange.
Reason (R): The preamble of FEMA states its aim to facilitate external trade and payments.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: FERA was a restrictive criminal law aimed at controlling outflow; it is FEMA that is a liberal civil law of management and regulation. R is true.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's forex reserves:
1. NRI deposits and loans from the World Bank form part of the reserves.
2. Foreign Currency Assets are the largest component and the Reserve Tranche Position the smallest.
3. The Reserve Tranche Position is a member's unconditional drawing right from its IMF quota.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: reserves are FCA, gold, SDRs and RTP; NRI deposits and foreign/World Bank loans are not reserves.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's forex reserves first crossed US$ 100 billion in December 2003.
2. In January 1991 the reserves had fallen to about US$ 12 billion.
3. Reserves of $682.3 billion on 29 May 2026 gave about 11 months of import cover.
4. The overall BoP surplus of $20.8 billion in July 2026 was driven by the RBI's special FCNR(B) deposit scheme.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 1991 low was about $1.2 billion (FCA below $1 billion, about two weeks of imports).

s:
Consider the following statements about India's current account:
1. India recorded its first current account surplus in 24 years in 2001-02.
2. The CAD peaked at about 4.8% of GDP in FY13, lower than the 1990-91 crisis level.
3. The CAD for FY 2025-26 was about $25.2 billion, around 0.6% of GDP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the FY13 peak of 4.8% (taper tantrum) was higher than the 1990-91 level of 3.1-3.2%.

s:
Match List-I (Country) with List-II (Remittance fact):
List-I | List-II
a. USA | i. Largest source for India (27.7%)
b. UAE | ii. Second-largest recipient in the world in 2024
c. United Kingdom | iii. Second-largest source for India (19.2%)
d. Mexico | iv. Third-largest source for India (10.8%)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: RBI survey 2023-24: USA 27.7% > UAE 19.2% > UK 10.8%. World Bank 2024: India ($129 bn) was the largest recipient, followed by Mexico ($68 bn).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The record services surplus of $188.8 billion in FY25 financed about two-thirds of the merchandise deficit.
2. Software services are the largest part of India's services surplus.
3. India's services exports rose to about USD 341.06 billion in FY 2023-24.
4. India's remittance receipts of $135.4 billion in FY25 were about 5.3% of GDP.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: $135.4 billion was about 3.5% of GDP.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Net primary income is a net inflow in India's invisibles.
Reason (R): Remittances are counter-cyclical and create no debt or repayment obligation.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: net primary income (interest, dividends, profits) is an outflow for India. R is true.

s:
Consider the following statements about measures to correct a BoP deficit:
1. Devaluation is an expenditure-switching measure.
2. A tight monetary policy with higher interest rates is an expenditure-switching measure.
3. Raising the import duty on gold is an expenditure-switching measure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: tight monetary policy (like tight fiscal policy) is expenditure-reducing.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Increasing government spending on domestic projects does not ordinarily correct a BoP deficit.
Reason (R): Encouraging FDI finances a BoP deficit rather than correcting it.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: higher government spending fails because it raises demand and imports; the FDI point is a separate fact.

s:
Match List-I (SDR basket currency, from 1 August 2022) with List-II (Weight):
List-I | List-II
a. US dollar | i. 43.38%
b. Euro | ii. 12.28%
c. Chinese renminbi | iii. 7.59%
d. Japanese yen | iv. 29.31%
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: US dollar 43.38%, euro 29.31%, renminbi 12.28%, yen 7.59% (pound sterling 7.44%) – five currencies in all.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The IMF's Rapid Credit Facility gives concessional support to low-income countries.
2. The Stand-By Arrangement and the Extended Fund Facility are regular IMF lending windows.
3. The Special Rupee Vostro Account is an IMF facility.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (like RBI swaps and the SAARC swap framework) are not IMF instruments.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The IMF acts as lender of last resort to a country whose reserves cannot cover its BoP deficit.
2. India drew on the IMF in 1991 to tide over its BoP crisis.
3. Concessional lending to low-income countries is the IMF's core function.
4. The SDR valuation basket has five currencies.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the IMF's core function is surveillance; concessional lending is one facility.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's external debt at end-June 2026:
1. The debt-to-GDP ratio was 29.8%.
2. Total external debt was about $778.2 billion.
3. The US dollar had the largest currency share.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the debt-to-GDP ratio was 20.8%; 29.8% is the rupee's share in the debt (dollar 54.8%).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve and a strong dollar tend to weaken the rupee.
Reason (R): Higher US yields draw hot money away from emerging markets.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: higher US yields pull hot money (FPI, debt flows) out of emerging markets, so the rupee weakens; dependence on such money raises vulnerability.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. During the 2013 taper tantrum, Morgan Stanley placed India among the 'Fragile Five'.
2. In FY 2025-26, FPIs pulled out about $16.4 billion while net FDI was only $6.9 billion.
3. FCNR(B) deposits and ECBs are regarded as self-sustaining inflows, unlike FDI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: FCNR(B) and ECB inflows are temporary; FDI is the flow expected to support a self-sustaining capital surplus.

s:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Devaluation | i. Market-driven fall in value under a flexible regime
b. Revaluation | ii. Official rise in value under a fixed regime
c. Appreciation | iii. Market-driven rise in value under a flexible regime
d. Depreciation | iv. Official reduction of value under a fixed regime
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Devaluation/revaluation are official changes under a fixed regime made by the government or monetary authority; appreciation/depreciation are market-driven (demand and supply) changes under a flexible regime.

s:
Consider the following statements about devaluation:
1. It is an expenditure-switching policy, making domestic goods cheaper for foreigners and imports costlier at home.
2. It raises the foreign-currency prices of a country's exports.
3. Imported inflation can limit the improvement in the trade balance that follows it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: devaluation lowers the foreign-currency price of exports, which is how it promotes them.

s:
Consider the following statements about the rupee's devaluations:
1. The first devaluation, in September 1949 along with sterling, was of about 30.5%.
2. In June 1966 the rupee lost about 57.5% of its value (₹4.76 to ₹7.50 per US$).
3. The July 1991 devaluation was carried out in two steps, on 1 and 2 July.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the rupee lost about 36.5% in 1966; 57.5% is the rise in the dollar's rupee price. 3 is wrong: the 1991 steps were on 1 and 3 July.

s:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Direct quote | i. Units of foreign currency per unit of domestic currency
b. Indirect quote | ii. Rate agreed now for delivery on a future date
c. Spot rate | iii. Immediate delivery, settled within two days
d. Forward rate | iv. Units of domestic currency per unit of foreign currency
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Direct quote – domestic currency per unit of foreign currency (₹95 = $1); indirect quote – the reverse; spot – immediate delivery within two days; forward – agreed now for future delivery.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Covering exchange-rate risk through a forward contract, as an importer does, is called hedging.
2. Taking an open position on expected exchange-rate moves is called arbitrage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: an open position on expected moves is speculation; arbitrage is buying a currency where it is cheaper and simultaneously selling it where it is dearer.

s:
Consider the following statements about exchange-rate regimes:
1. Under a fixed (pegged) system the central bank buys or sells foreign currency to hold the rate.
2. A managed float is market-determined with central-bank intervention when necessary – India's system.
3. Argentina's currency board of 1991 – January 2002 is classed as an intermediate regime.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: in the post-Bretton Woods classes, currency boards (like currency unions and pegs) are fixed regimes; bands and crawling pegs are intermediate.

s:
Match List-I (Concept) with List-II (Description):
List-I | List-II
a. Dutch disease | i. Deliberate undervaluation of a currency, as alleged of China
b. Carry trade | ii. Capital drawn in by a repo-rate hike
c. Currency manipulation | iii. Large capital inflows causing currency appreciation
d. Impossible trinity | iv. Fixed rate, free capital flows and independent monetary policy cannot all coexist
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Dutch disease – appreciation from large inflows; carry trade – capital attracted by higher rates (repo hike); currency manipulation – deliberate undervaluation; impossible trinity – fixed rate, free capital flows and independent monetary policy cannot coexist.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Higher imports can be accompanied by a stable or even appreciating rupee.
Reason (R): Large net investment inflows raise the supply of foreign currency and tend to make the currency appreciate.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: when higher imports are backed by net investment inflows, the extra supply of dollars offsets the import demand.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Purchasing Power Parity theory links the long-run exchange rate to the inflation differential between countries.
2. The Economic Survey 2025-26 names PPP, the savings-investment balance and the current account as long-run anchors of the exchange rate.
3. The impossible trinity is also called the Mundell-Fleming trilemma.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct as given in the notes.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bretton Woods Conference was held on 1-22 July 1944 in New Hampshire, USA.
2. 44 nations took part in it.
3. It set up the IMF and the IBRD and fixed exchange rates centred on the US dollar.
4. The IMF was formally created on 27 December 1944.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the IMF was formally created on 27 December 1945, with India a founding member.

s:
Consider the following statements about the IMF:
1. India's quota is about 2.75% of total SDR quotas (March 2026).
2. Liechtenstein became its 191st member in October 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: India's quota is 2.75% (votes 2.63%), and Liechtenstein became the 191st member in October 2024.

s:
Match List-I (Year) with List-II (Exchange-rate step):
List-I | List-II
a. 1971 | i. Smithsonian Agreement
b. September 1975 | ii. Rates unified and market-determined
c. 1 March 1993 | iii. IMF Article VIII accepted – current account convertibility
d. August 1994 | iv. Rupee delinked from sterling and pegged to a basket
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 1971 – Smithsonian Agreement; September 1975 – rupee pegged to a basket of currencies; 1 March 1993 – LERMS dual rates unified; August 1994 – Article VIII, current account convertibility.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. FEMA was first proposed in the Union Budget of 1997-98.
2. A two-year sunset clause for FERA cases ended on 31 May 2002.
3. The second Tarapore Committee, on Fuller Capital Account Convertibility, was appointed in 1997.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Tarapore I was 1997; Tarapore II on fuller capital account convertibility was appointed in 2006 (report 31 July 2006).

s:
Consider the following statements about Special Drawing Rights:
1. The IMF created SDRs in 1969 to supplement members' official reserves.
2. SDRs exist only as book-keeping entries.
3. The renminbi has been in the SDR basket since 1 October 2016.
4. The largest general allocation of SDRs, about $650 billion, was made in August 2009.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the largest allocation of about $650 billion was made in August 2021.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Reserve Tranche Position (RTP):
1. It was historically known as the gold tranche and can be drawn from the IMF without conditions.
2. It is the largest component of India's foreign exchange reserves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the RTP is the smallest component (FCA > gold > SDR > RTP).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The RBI is the custodian of India's foreign exchange reserves.
2. In September 2026 India overtook Japan to become the fourth-largest holder of forex reserves.
3. The India-Japan bilateral swap renewed from 28 February 2026 is a two-way arrangement in local currencies against US dollars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: at $785.71 billion on 15 September 2026 India overtook Russia, not Japan, to rank fourth.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The RBI compiles trade-weighted NEER/REER indices for baskets of 40 and 6 currencies.
2. The base year of these indices is 2004-05 = 100.
3. The REER is the NEER adjusted for relative inflation differentials.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the base is 2015-16 = 100.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): A high REER suggests that the rupee is overvalued.
Reason (R): A rise in the REER improves a country's export competitiveness.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: a rise in REER means a loss of competitiveness (overvalued, less competitive rupee), not an improvement.

s:
Match List-I (RBI tool) with List-II (Example):
List-I | List-II
a. Spot intervention | i. Selling dollars from reserves
b. Forex buy/sell swap | ii. Banks sell dollars to the RBI and buy them back later at a premium
c. NDF curbs | iii. RBI bearing the full hedging cost on fresh deposits till 30 September 2026
d. FCNR(B) support | iv. Restricting domestic banks in offshore markets and Net Open Position limits
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Spot – selling dollars from reserves; swap – banks sell dollars to the RBI and buy back at a premium; NDF curbs – restricting banks in offshore Non-Deliverable Forward markets with NOP limits; FCNR(B) – RBI bore the hedging cost till 30 September 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The primary aim of RBI intervention in the forex market is to defend a fixed level of the rupee.
2. Import curbs and export promotion are Government structural measures rather than RBI exchange-rate tools.
3. In FY 2025-26 up to January 2026 the rupee depreciated by about 5.4%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the RBI aims to curb excessive volatility, not to defend a fixed level.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The RBI framework for invoicing and settling trade in rupees came in July 2022 and was built into the Foreign Trade Policy 2023.
2. Special Rupee Vostro Accounts are rupee accounts of Indian banks maintained with foreign banks.
3. Since 2025, surplus balances in Special Rupee Vostro Accounts may be invested in corporate bonds and commercial papers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: SRVAs are foreign banks' rupee accounts with Indian banks (a vostro is a foreign bank's account with a domestic bank; a nostro is ours abroad).

s:
Consider the following statements about the SAARC Currency Swap Framework:
1. It was instituted by the RBI in 2012.
2. A swap has a tenor of 3 months, rollable twice.
3. The 2024-27 framework has an INR window of ₹250 billion.
4. The first INR drawdown under it was made by Sri Lanka in April 2026.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the first INR drawdown was by the Maldives in April 2026.

s:
Match List-I (Bond) with List-II (Feature):
List-I | List-II
a. Masala bond | i. Rupee-denominated, issued abroad
b. Samurai bond | ii. Yuan bond, China
c. Panda bond | iii. Issued by SBI in 1998 in US dollar, sterling and Deutsche Mark
d. Resurgent India Bonds | iv. Yen bond, Japan
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Masala – rupee-denominated bond issued abroad; Samurai – yen bond (Japan); Panda – yuan bond (China); Resurgent India Bonds – SBI, 5 August 1998.

s:
Consider the following statements about masala bonds:
1. The first masala bond was issued by the IFC in November 2014.
2. Maharashtra was the first Indian State to issue one, in 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Kerala was the first State to issue a masala bond (2019).

s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO:
1. It was created by the Marrakesh Agreement signed in April 1994.
2. It had 166 members as of April 2026; Afghanistan became the 164th member in July 2016.
3. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria is its sixth Director-General.
4. It came into being on 1 January 1995.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Okonjo-Iweala is the 7th DG (and first woman, from 1 March 2021); Roberto Azevedo was the 6th.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Uruguay Round:
1. It was the eighth GATT round, launched in September 1986 at Punta del Este.
2. 123 contracting parties took part in it.
3. It was concluded in December 1993.
4. Its Draft Final Act, the Dunkel Draft, was tabled on 20 October 1991.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the Dunkel Draft (Draft Final Act) was tabled on 20 December 1991; '20 October' is a misprint in some guides.

s:
Match List-I (Subsidy box under the AoA) with List-II (Covers):
List-I | List-II
a. Green Box | i. Price-linked support such as MSP, measured as AMS
b. Blue Box | ii. Research, pest and disease control, public stockholding for food security
c. Amber Box | iii. Special and differential support for developing countries
d. S&D Box | iv. Direct payments under production-limiting programmes
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Green – minimal-distortion support (research, pest control, PSH) with no limits; Blue – 'amber with conditions', production-limiting direct payments exempt from reduction; Amber – MSP, input subsidies (AMS) to be cut to de minimis; S&D – developing-country support.

s:
Match List-I (AoA rule) with List-II (Commitment):
List-I | List-II
a. De minimis limit | i. 24% over 10 years
b. Total AMS cut (developed) | ii. 5% (developed) and 10% (developing) of production value
c. Tariff cut (developing) | iii. 20% over 6 years
d. Export subsidy cut (developed) | iv. 36% by value or 21% by volume over 6 years
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: De minimis – 5%/10%; Total AMS – 20% over 6 years for developed (13.3% over 10 for developing); tariffs – 24% over 10 years for developing (36% over 6 for developed); export subsidies – 36% by value or 21% by volume over 6 years (developed).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Agreement on Agriculture:
1. Conversion of non-tariff barriers into tariffs is called tariffication.
2. Blue Box payments may be based on 85% or less of base production.
3. Amber Box support is exempt from reduction commitments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Amber Box support is trade-distorting and is to be reduced to de minimis; it is the Blue Box that is exempt from reduction.

s:
Match List-I (WTO agreement) with List-II (India / content):
List-I | List-II
a. TRIPS | i. Liberalisation commitments in trade in services
b. SPS / TBT | ii. Ratified by India in April 2016
c. Trade Facilitation Agreement | iii. Patents Act amendment of 2005 – product patents
d. GATS | iv. Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: TRIPS – product patents via the 2005 Patents amendment; SPS/TBT – FSS Act 2006; TFA (Bali 2013) – ratified April 2016; GATS – trade in services.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Codex Alimentarius Commission was set up by the FAO and WHO in 1963.
2. India relies on the Lisbon Agreement for protecting geographical indications.
3. India's Patents Act, in force from 1972, was based on the N. Rajagopala Ayyangar Committee report.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: India is not in the Lisbon Agreement; it protects GIs under TRIPS through the GI Act 1999.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Under the WTO SCM Agreement, subsidies for research and development, regional development and environmental purposes are non-actionable.
Reason (R): Under the SCM Agreement, 'red light' subsidies are actionable subsidies open to countervailing duty.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: 'red light' subsidies are prohibited; actionable subsidies are the ones that can attract countervailing duty.

s:
Match List-I (WTO Ministerial Conference) with List-II (Outcome):
List-I | List-II
a. MC4 Doha, 2001 | i. Duty-free quota-free access for LDCs
b. MC5 Cancun, 2003 | ii. Collapsed; G-33 formed
c. MC6 Hong Kong, 2005 | iii. Doha Development Agenda launched
d. MC10 Nairobi, 2015 | iv. Elimination of agricultural export subsidies
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: MC4 Doha 2001 – Doha Development Agenda; MC5 Cancun 2003 – collapsed, G-33 formed; MC6 Hong Kong 2005 – DFQF for LDCs; MC10 Nairobi 2015 – elimination of farm export subsidies (first MC in Africa).

s:
Match List-I (Ministerial Conference) with List-II (Venue):
List-I | List-II
a. MC1 (1996) | i. Buenos Aires
b. MC3 (1999) | ii. Seattle
c. MC11 (2017) | iii. Abu Dhabi
d. MC13 (2024) | iv. Singapore
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: MC1 – Singapore 1996; MC3 – Seattle 1999 (collapsed amid protests); MC11 – Buenos Aires 2017; MC13 – Abu Dhabi 2024.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. MC12 at Geneva (June 2022) adopted the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement and the COVID-19 TRIPS waiver.
2. MC14 was held at Yaounde, Cameroon, in March 2026.
3. At MC14 India supported adding the Investment Facilitation for Development Agreement to Annex 4.
4. A permanent solution on public stockholding was achieved at MC14.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: India blocked adding the IFD to Annex 4 though 129 of 166 members backed it. 4 is wrong: MC14 ended without a declaration and no PSH solution.

s:
Consider the following statements about WTO groupings:
1. The G-33, formed in 2003, focuses on food security, the Special Safeguard Mechanism and special products.
2. The G-90 comprises the African Group, ACP countries and LDCs.
3. The Special Safeguard Mechanism lets developing countries raise tariffs permanently against import surges.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the SSM allows tariffs to be raised only for a short time against import surges or price falls.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Peace Clause:
1. Adopted at Bali (MC9, 2013), it shields food-security public stockholding even if it breaches de minimis or AMS limits.
2. It applies only to existing programmes and traditional staples and requires notification.
3. India was the first to invoke it, for wheat, in 2020.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: India invoked it first for rice (2020, for marketing year 2018-19).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): India argues that its MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is wrongly shown as a large Amber Box subsidy.
Reason (R): The support is calculated against an outdated historical reference price of 1986-88.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: measuring MSP support against the 1986-88 reference price inflates the calculated Amber Box support.

s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies:
1. It was adopted at MC12 in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025.
2. It also covers aquaculture and inland fishing.
3. It is the first WTO agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the agreement covers marine wild capture; aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India became the 123rd member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance of the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement in July 2026.
2. Phase 2 of the fisheries talks (overcapacity and overfishing) was deferred at MC14 to the General Council in Geneva.
3. The TFA and the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement are the only two new multilateral WTO agreements in 30 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct as given in the notes.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): India is wary of plurilateral initiatives such as the IFD and the E-Commerce Agreement.
Reason (R): The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions lapsed on 31 March 2026.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: India's concern is that plurilaterals may fragment the WTO by moving away from consensus.

s:
Match List-I (WTO dispute against India) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. DS456 (USA) | i. Sugarcane prices and export subsidies
b. DS541 (USA) | ii. Solar cells – domestic content
c. Brazil, Australia, Guatemala | iii. Duties on phones and ICT goods
d. EU, Japan, Taiwan | iv. Export subsidies under MEIS, SEZ, EOU
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: DS456 – solar cells (India lost 2016); DS541 – MEIS/SEZ/EOU export subsidies (2019); sugar – Brazil, Australia, Guatemala (2021); ICT tariffs – EU, Japan, Taiwan (2023).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India has joined the EU-led Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement set up in 2020.
2. The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019 because the USA blocked appointments.
3. The BRICS New Delhi Declaration (September 2026) sought restoration of the WTO Appellate Body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: India has not joined the MPIA, the EU-led stop-gap.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Investment by a person resident outside India in an unlisted Indian company counts as FDI only if it is 10% or more of the equity.
2. Foreign investment of 10% or more of the post-issue paid-up equity of a listed company is generally classed as FDI.
3. The 10% threshold separating FDI from FPI is based on the Arvind Mayaram Committee's recommendation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: in an unlisted company any stake bought by a person resident outside India is FDI, whatever its size.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Hyundai's facility at Sriperumbudur is an example of greenfield FDI.
Reason (R): Greenfield investment means acquiring an existing enterprise, as Vodafone did with Hutchison Essar.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: greenfield means building a new facility; acquiring an existing firm (Vodafone–Hutchison Essar) is brownfield FDI.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. FDI is generally long-term and may carry management control, whereas FPI is liquid and short-term.
2. Foreign Portfolio Investors in India must register with SEBI.
3. The SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 kept QFIs outside the FPI framework.
4. Foreign Portfolio Investment was opened to India in 1992.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the 2019 Regulations unified FIIs, sub-accounts and QFIs as FPIs.

s:
Match List-I (Form of foreign capital) with List-II (Classification):
List-I | List-II
a. External commercial borrowing | i. Banking capital
b. NRI deposits (FCNR(B), NRE) | ii. Debt
c. ADR / GDR | iii. Offshore derivative instruments
d. Participatory Notes | iv. Portfolio investment in BoP data
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ECB (like trade credit and FCCB) – debt; NRI deposits – banking capital; ADRs/GDRs – equity raised abroad, counted as portfolio investment in the BoP; P-Notes – offshore derivative instruments issued by registered FPIs.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): External Commercial Borrowings in India are regulated by SEBI.
Reason (R): ECBs, trade credit and Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds are debt forms of foreign capital.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: ECBs are regulated by the RBI under FEMA. R is true: ECB, trade credit and FCCB are classed as debt.

s:
Consider the following statements about FDI routes:
1. Under the automatic route no prior approval is needed, only post-facto reporting to the RBI.
2. Since the FIPB was abolished in June 2017, Government-route proposals are filed on the Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal.
3. All sectors are now on the automatic route.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: India follows a negative-list approach with over 90% of sectors automatic – not all (e.g. multi-brand retail and PSBs need Government approval).

s:
Match List-I (Sector) with List-II (FDI limit, 2026):
List-I | List-II
a. Defence (automatic route) | i. 20%
b. Public sector banks | ii. 49%
c. Scheduled civil aviation (automatic, non-NRI) | iii. 100%
d. Telecom | iv. 74%
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Defence – 74% automatic (up to 100% Government route); PSBs – 20%, Government route; scheduled civil aviation – 49% automatic for non-NRIs (100% in all); telecom – 100% automatic.

s:
Consider the following statements about FDI caps:
1. Foreign investment in private-sector banks is capped at 74%.
2. FDI in brownfield pharmaceutical projects is allowed up to 74% under the automatic route.
3. FDI in trading, including e-commerce, of food products made in India is allowed up to 100% under the automatic route.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: 100% FDI in trading of food products made in India is through the Government route.

s:
With reference to FDI in e-commerce in India, consider the following statements:
1. 100% FDI under the automatic route is allowed in the marketplace model.
2. From July 2026, FDI in the inventory model is allowed where the inventory is used to export domestically manufactured goods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the marketplace model allows 100% automatic FDI; the inventory model is otherwise barred, but since July 2026 it is allowed for exporting domestically made goods.

s:
Consider the following activities:
1. Manufacture of cigars and cigarettes of tobacco
2. Trading in Transferable Development Rights
3. Railway infrastructure
4. Nidhi companies
In how many of the above is FDI prohibited in India?
x: Three – 1, 2 and 4 are prohibited (with lottery, gambling, chit funds, real estate business, atomic energy and railway operations). 3 is not: railway infrastructure allows 100% FDI under the automatic route.

s:
Consider the following statements about FDI into India:
1. In FY 2024-25 Singapore was the top source with about 30%, followed by Mauritius.
2. The United States was the third-largest source in FY 2024-25.
3. According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, financial services had the largest share within services FDI during FY23-FY25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct (Singapore 30% > Mauritius 17% > US 11%). 3 is wrong: services were 80.2% of FDI, and information and communication had the largest share (25.8%).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's net FDI peaked at $44.0 billion in 2020-21.
2. In FY 2024-25 gross FDI was about $81 billion but net FDI only about $353 million.
3. FY 2025-26 saw a record gross FDI of $94.6 billion.
4. Profit repatriation, outward FDI and PE/VC exits keep net FDI weak despite high gross inflows.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: All four are correct as given in the notes.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the first half of FY 2025-26 the top three states by FDI were Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat.
2. During April 2000 – March 2015 the RBI's Mumbai regional office received the largest cumulative FDI.
3. Google announced a $15 billion, 1 GW AI data centre at Visakhapatnam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: in H1 FY26 the order was Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu (Gujarat was third in FY 2022-23).

s:
Consider the following statements about FPI in debt and equity:
1. Under the General Route, FPIs may hold up to 6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 2% of State Government securities.
2. Under the RBI framework of November 2024, FPI holdings above 10% of a listed company's equity can be reclassified as FDI.
3. India's target weight in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index is 15%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: India's target weight in the JP Morgan EM bond index is 10%; 15% is the FPI limit in corporate bonds (Budget 2020-21).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): FPI flows into India are volatile, with outflows of about ₹2.2 lakh crore in FY 2025-26.
Reason (R): FPI flows are significantly influenced by US Federal Reserve interest rates and global risk appetite.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: FPI is liquid 'hot money' driven by US rates and global risk appetite, hence large swings such as the FY26 outflow.

s:
Consider the following statements about Press Note 3:
1. Since April 2020, all FDI from a country sharing a land border with India needs the Government route.
2. It covers Sri Lanka and Bhutan.
3. Under the March 2026 amendment, effective 1 May 2026, firms with up to 10% Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership (defined as per the PML Rules, 2005) may use the automatic route.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Bhutan is covered (land border) but Sri Lanka is not.

s:
Match List-I (Agreement) with List-II (Came into force):
List-I | List-II
a. SAFTA | i. 1 May 2022
b. ASEAN-India FTA (goods) | ii. 2010
c. India-UAE CEPA | iii. 29 December 2022
d. India-Australia ECTA | iv. 2006
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: SAFTA – 2006; ASEAN-India FTA in goods – 2010; India-UAE CEPA – 1 May 2022; India-Australia ECTA – 29 December 2022.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RCEP:
1. It was signed on 15 November 2020 by 15 members.
2. It came into force on 1 January 2022.
3. India is one of its founding members.
4. India's trade deficit with China, a key reason for staying out, was $53.5 billion in 2018-19.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: India opted out in 2019 over China's market dominance and the trade deficit, and is not a member.
